title: Getting Started
contentHtml: Before beginning a shared activity, pause and look around the work area. Check that the space is clear, the equipment appears undamaged, and the instructions are available. If something is unclear, ask the person leading the activity before continuing.

title: Spotting a Concern
contentHtml: A concern is a condition that could make an activity unsafe or difficult. Examples in this fictional lesson include a blocked walkway, a loose cable, or a damaged tool. Do not ignore the concern. Keep a safe distance and let the activity lead know what you noticed.

title: Choosing a Next Step
contentHtml: A simple control can reduce the chance of harm. Depending on the situation, the activity lead may clear the area, replace equipment, or explain a safer method. Follow the agreed instructions and check that the concern has been addressed before work resumes.

title: Sharing Feedback
contentHtml: A study assistant can explain feedback after a qualified person has reviewed a response. The assistant does not decide whether the response is correct. It can point the learner back to the relevant lesson and explain the idea in different words.
